nar.text: Because of the dust from the dirt roads, the cars were started individually, at intervals of one minute.
The starter Fabio Vecchioni, commissioner of the R.A.C.I. was ready for the 9:00 AM start and released the first car which was Natali's Alfa Romeo with the lowest number four.
Because of the dust from the dirt roads, the cars were started individually, at intervals of one minute.
The starter Fabio Vecchioni, commissioner of the R.A.C.I. was ready for the 9:00 AM start and released the first car which was Natali's Alfa Romeo with the lowest number four.
Brilli Peri's Talbot was the first to appear at the end of the first lap in 50m31.4s at an average speed of 73.392 km/h.
Stuck in the Austro Daimler drove the second best time and Campari in the Alfa Romeo was third.
Borzacchini stopped at his pit for one minute to change a rear wheel.
Natali, Arcangeli, Corinaldi and Di Stefano all fail to complete the first lap.

Brilli Peri laps in 50m12.8s on the second lap.
Borzacchini stops to have his brakes fixed and falls from fifth to 21st.
Stuck drove an outstanding race and it appeared that he could even threaten Brilli Peri, if his engine would withstand the strain.
When Nenzioni crashed his Maserati and Fagioli retired his Salmson with broken brakes after two laps, the field was down to 26 cars

Brilli Peri is back in front at the end of lap four; his lap including the stop took 56m05s.
The German Stuck failed to appear at the end of the fourth lap. Later it became known that he had left the road without greater harm.
Allgemeine Automobil-Zeitung (Wien) reported that Stuck's race ended when his Austro Daimler hit the wall of a bridge due to dust kicked up by another competitor.

When Rosa retired, the field was down to 19 cars.
Ernesto Maserati stopped at his pit, too sick to carry on, so his brother Alfieri took over for the last lap.
Brilli Peri wins in 5h10m57.6s.
Sartorio overtook De Sterlich on the last lap and beat him by just 6 seconds after almost six hours at the wheel.
